characters.name: Johnston Green
characters.description: Wasteland Elder: In the aftermath of a series of nuclear bombings, small-town Colorado mayor and retired Army Ranger Johnston Greene struggles to keep his town safe and stable amidst threats like nuclear fallout, the cessation of outside food shipments, andTrigger-Happylooters. Even after he's voted out of office in favor of a more gung-ho rival, Johnston remains a force for wisdom and stability.

characters.name: Gail Green
characters.description: Fiery Redhead: She is a caring yet determined and outspoken woman with dyed red hair. The Apocalypse Brings Out the Best in People: He goes from aBlack Sheepwith aDark and Troubled Pastto the hero of the town. Dark and Troubled Past: He has been involved in a heist crew where his girlfriend’s daughter died filling in for him andPrivate Military Contractorsbefore coming home and trying to make something better.

characters.name: Eric Green
characters.description: Took a Level in Badass: He starts out as a useful but overshadowed bureaucrat in an unhappy marriage before gradually becoming occasionalBash Brotherswith Jake in fire fights, the one to first uncover the aggression in New Bern, willing to face Constantino down during aggressive negotiations, and a reliable figure in all the struggles.

characters.name: April Green
characters.description: The Cobbler's Children Have No Shoes: She is the town doctor but isImperiled in Pregnancybecause there isNo Healthcare in the Apocalypse.

characters.name: Stanley Richmond
characters.description: The eldest of the Richmond family and head of the household after the death of his parents.

characters.name: Bonnie Richmond
characters.description: Stanley's hearing-impaired little sister. All Girls Want Bad Boys: She is drawn to a handsome yet brash and dishonest skater. Handicapped Badass: Goetz sends some of his men to kill Bonnie because she has evidence of his embezzling. Despite being a deaf, rural farmgirl, she picks up a shotgun and manages to kill most of the men sent to kill her before she finally goes down.

characters.name: Robert Hawkins
characters.description: Chekhov's Gunman: He only has one scene in the pilot, suggesting the sheriff take steps to keep any bandits on the road from knowing the town is still standing. Good All Along: Initially set up as a potential accomplice of the bombing plot, he was actually an infiltrator trying to stop it. Scary Black Man: He is an often intense African-American newcomer hiding secrets with national implications even from his own family.

characters.name: Darcy Hawkins
characters.description: Took a Level in Badass: She goes from frightened and disgusted with the whole conspiracy she is caught up in to assisting her husband in solving things by season 2.

characters.name: Allison Hawkins
characters.description: The elder daughter of Robert and Darcy Hawkins. I Did What I Had to Do: Allison seems to suffer no emotional trauma after shooting Sarah while the latter was trying to kill Robert, and simply accepts it as doing what had to be done. This is in spite of her being a teenager with no prior combat experience and by no means beingThe Stoicas she reflected on dead loved ones. Little Miss Badass: Allison adaptsvery wellto life after the collapse of social order, much to her mother's chagrin. After learning how to shoot a gun, she doesn't hesitate to kill to save her father's life, and is able to justify it because she did what was necessary to protect her family.

characters.name: Emily Sullivan
characters.description: White Sheep: Emily is an honest teacher, while her father and late brother are crooks.

characters.name: Heather Lisinski
characters.description: Wrench Wench: She's very technically knowledgeable, demonstrating detailed knowledge on how to repair air filtration systems, computers, and cars, just to name a few.

characters.name: Dale Turner
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: Dale is a shy, mild-mannered, soft-spoken young man that avoids confrontation, especially when the show first starts. This doesn't stop Dale from shooting an unarmed Mitch Cafferty when he finds out that the latter killed Gracie Leigh, his surrogate mother. From Nobody to Nightmare: Before the bombs, Dale started out as the town loser living in a trailer park and working at the general store. After the events of season 1, he's the major runner of trade in town, with an army behind him. By the end of season 2, he's the chief smuggler of controlled goods under J&R's nose, and is the leader of Jericho's organized 'crime' against J&R's tightly controlled commerce. My Parents Are Dead: Both of his parents were out of town when one of the bombs went off. Unfortunately, they were in one of the targeted cities. He finds out via avoicemail messagethey were leaving at the moment of the detonation.

characters.name: Gray Anderson
characters.description: Johnston's rival in the mayoral race. Internal Reformist: After the flaws of theASAbecome apparent, Gray still goes to serve in their Congress, hoping he can call attention to their more extreme methods and get people to rethink them. The series finale reveals that he's failed miserably, and he's quick to give up on the new government. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Takes every opportunity to try and garner the peoples' favor over Johnston Green in his bid to become mayor, even in the midst of the apocalypse. In spite of his constant jerkass behavior, Gray actuallydoesrespect Johnston and does care about the people of Jericho, he's just very bad at cooperating and handling himself under pressure. Offscreen Moment of Awesome: Gray has some tough and harrowing offscreen adventures while scouting the area in the first part of season 1. He comes home with tales of some frighteningApocalypse Anarchyand reports about which cities were destroyed by the nukes. Put on a Bus: Gray disappears from the show for two long periods of time, althoughThe Bus Came Backon each occasion. In season 1, he departs Jericho a few days after the bombs go off to scout the neighboring communities. Early in season 2, he goes to Cheyenne to serve in the new Congress.

characters.name: Mimi Clark
characters.description: An IRS agent from New York sent to Jericho in order to audit Stanley Richmond's farm. Badass Bureaucrat: Is able to carve through J&R's paperwork to expose someone embezzling money from the company, and is able to see through a bad deal given to Stanley regarding ownership of his farm. City Mouse: From a world of Starbucks, paperwork, taxis, and organization, to Jericho's small town of farms and having no practical skills in the nuclear apocalypse. After her and Stanley become a couple, she does what she can to adapt to her new situation. Mama Bear: Once she cares about someone, she will be very protective of them, such as when Bonnie is dating a boy in town, and watching out for Stanley in regards to J&R's predatory business offers regarding his farm. Skewed Priorities: Millions are dead, he entire country's social structure has collapsed, and everyone around her is facing starvation and death by bandits, and she continues hounding Stanley about the back taxes he owes the now non-existent IRS. Revealed later to be denial when she finds out Washington DC is destroyed, and collapses in grief that everything she's worked for is gone.

characters.name: Gracie Leigh
characters.description: Parental Substitute: Gracie treats Dale like a son and is closer to him than most in town. Following the death of his parents, she effectively becomes a sort of adoptive mother to him, even letting him sleep in her store.

characters.name: Kenchy Dhuwalia
characters.description: Lovable Coward: He has a decent moral compass and provides some comic relief, but will sometimes fold under pressure and threats, something that he's honest about. Open Heart Dentistry: He's a plastic surgeon, but must treat several people suffering from fever, gunshot wounds, strokes, or pregnancy complications. Not all of his patients survive.

characters.name: Fire Chief Carroll
characters.description: Dropped After the Pilot: He appears in the pilot as a minor yet notable town leader. Afterward, he's never seen again, with Gail briefly mentioning thathe and his men left towntotry to provide aid to the bomb victims in Denver.

characters.name: Jimmy Taylor
characters.description: Stout Strength: He is a chunky guy who is dependable in a fight and can shrug off some injuries in the second episode. Red Oni, Blue Oni: He is the blue to Bill’s red, having closer bonds with their neighbors and thinking more stuff through critically.

characters.name: Bill Koehler
characters.description: Red Oni, Blue Oni: He is the red to Jimmy’s blue, valuing stern order and logic over sentiment and gut feelings about people, although he is under a lot of pressure, has lines he won’t cross and can show a softer side around some people.

characters.name: John Goetz
characters.description: The Heavy: He represents the muscle of J&R (otherwise represented by offscreen officials and reasonable middle managers) and murders hospital doctors and patients while looting medication, enforces draconian laws in Jericho, and has his men kill Bonnie. Smug Snake: He is a gloating murderer eager to exploit his private army and corporate connections to avoid anything bad. Stealing from the Till: He shamelessly embezzled from his bosses.

characters.name: Mitch Cafferty
characters.description: Asshole Victim:Dale shoots Mitch dead after he reveals to the former that he killed Gracie and had tried to threaten and extort him. It's safe to say nobody missed him. Jerk with a Heart of Jerk: He is a particularly odious career criminal who seems to have anEven Evil Has Standardsmoments after it looks like Jonah killedGracie Leigh, only for it to turn out that he's the one who killed her. The Star Scream: He frames Jonah for murder to try and usurp his leadership. Villain Ball: Tries threatening Dale by revealing that he was the one who killed Gracie, when he might have otherwise gotten away with it due to lack of witnesses. Needless to say, it doesn't end well.

characters.name: Jonah Prowse
characters.description: Emily's estranged father and a convicted criminal who goes from minor gang leader to recurring antagonist after the attacks. Archnemesis Dad: Played with. He and Emily were on poor terms even before the attacks, and things don't improve much after, given how much of a problem his gang is. However, Jonah doesn't seem to have any ill will towards his daughter. Not Me This Time: While he is a career criminal, Gracie's murder was one crime he definitely wasn't guilty of. His track record means that most people are quick to believe his guilt. Screw This, I'm Outta Here: He gets the hell out of Dodge in the leadup to the clash between Jericho and New Bern, outright warning of a bloodbath. What Happened to the Mouse?: He's completely absent from Season 2, and given the restoration of law and order and crackdowns on bandits, as Major Beck explicitly states destroying at least one such operation, his fate is left up in the air.

characters.name: Phil Constantino
characters.description: Before the bombs, he was Sheriff of the city of New Bern. Through a coup, he became mayor as well, and turned into an aspiring dictator. He's the primary antagonist of season 1, with plans to invade Jericho. Evil Counterpart: For Johnston Green and Gray Anderson, in that he's the leader who pulled his town together after the crisis like Johnston, and is politically ambitious like Gray Anderson, but without the level-headedness of Johnston or conscience of Anderson. The Revolution Will Not Be Civilized: After the AS Army moves in, runs a terrorist group against them, as opposed to Jericho's more civilized relationship with them.

characters.name: Maggie Mullen
characters.description: Before the bombs, she was an ordinary grad student working on her Dissertation in Russian Literature. After the bombs, she was a starving refugee who joined a group posing as US Marines in order con people out of food and survive. She is later seen in New Bern as one of their prisoners. Alliterative Name:MaggieMullen. Heel–Face Turn: Maggie goes from a forcedCon Artistjust to survive to pulling cons on New Bern's leadership to help out Jericho by helping Jake and Eric escape. Heel–Face Door-Slam: She helps the people from Jericho escape New Bern, and gets severely injured for her troubles. Whatever Happened to the Mouse?: After her injuries, she disappears from the show.

characters.name: Edward Beck
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: He's aReasonable Authority Figure, but he goes fullInspector Javertfollowing the murder of the sociopathic Goetz. Obliviously Evil: He acts as the local representative of the season 2 antagonists but doesn't realize that they're the antagonists, andturns on them once they do.

characters.name: Russell
characters.description: Anti-Villain: He assists the antagonistic Constantino, but never happily and never with anything particularly bad. In his first episode, he even saves several of the main characters from being lynched by a third antagonistic faction. Mr. Exposition: He provides severalInfo Dumpsabout the state of affairs in New Bern, and is the first one to describe how the country is now theDivided States of America. Noble Top Enforcer: Russell assists Constantino, who is a major enemy of Jericho. However, he constantly attempts to broker truces between Jericho and New Bern, and is especially concerned about trying to keep his old friend Heather from being killed.

characters.name: Thomas Valente
characters.description: Bald of Evil: Whilenot the mastermind of the attacks, contrary to implications, he cares more about protecting corporate interests and his own skin than his fellow Americans and his bald head makes him recognizable in satellite photos. Greater-Scope Villain: He is responsible for a lot of how the ASA is consolidating into a dictatorship and is the one to first send its forces to Jericho, but he only appears in a few flashbacks, video images, or livestreams.

characters.name: John Smith
characters.description: Mysterious Informant: He spends most of season 2 as a voice in a radio providing information about the conspiracy and advice on what to do. Eventually, it becomes clear he would have had to set off the bombs himself to know so much. Western Terrorists: He sought to blow up the fifty biggest cities in the country to rid American society of corporate dominance.

characters.name: Sarah Mason
characters.description: Chronic Backstabbing Disorder: She betrayed the other agents on her team to help kill them and set off the bombs and then betrays them to try and get the bomb for her own profit.

characters.name: Chavez
characters.description: Hero of Another Story: He's a member of Hawkins' team of spies and is first mentioned about halfway through season one, but spends most of the series offscreen having adventures of his own. He only shows up in person for a few episodes of season 2. Properly Paranoid: He mentions that he never trusted Sarah, who turns out to be a traitor.

characters.name: Trish Merrick
characters.description: Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: Trish is blonde, compassionate, and well-intentioned. Hidden Depths: She's fluent in sign language and quickly befriends Bonnie. Honest Corporate Executive: Trish is a low-ranking business executive at a thoroughly corrupt company, but is pretty benevolent herself. She tries to help the people of Jericho during her time in town, orders Goetz to put a stop to his embezzling, and fires Goetz (cancelling his protection from prosecution) after he kills Bonnie. Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!: She's horrified when her attempts to intimidate Goetz into abandoning his embezzlement scheme cause him to kill Bonnie in an effort to get rid of the evidence. Put on a Bus: She and her coworkers are pulled out of town in the penultimate episode after Stanley kills Goetz.

characters.name: Roger Hammond
characters.description: Hidden Depths: While mainly treated as aDisposable Fiancéeto Emily, he has someTrue Companionsloyalty to his fellow plain crash survivors and almost happily goes into exile over actions done on their behalf. Uncertain Doom: He ends up leaving Jericho in the direction of New Bern, but characters from there make no mention of Roger. It's left unclear if he made it, moved on, or even survived the trek there at all.

characters.name: Victor Miller
characters.description: All for Nothing:The refugees he tried to save all die of radiation poisoning shortly after he does, rendering his efforts pointless. No Good Deed Goes Unpunished: He went back to Denver against the plan Hawkins' group had agreed on in order to save a group of refugees. Not only does he get a lethal dose of radiation,all of the refugees die of radiation poisoning too. We Hardly Knew Ye: Dies of radiation poisoning in the same episode that he's introduced.
